### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. retinitis pigmentosa 61  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:12605)

**Proposed mechanism:** CLRN1 (HGNC:12605) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (REACT:R-HSA-201883); Endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (REACT:R-HSA-201883) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000506); CLRN1 (HGNC:12605) —DISRUPTS→ Endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (REACT:R-HSA-201883); Endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein degradation (ERAD) (REACT:R-HSA-201883) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000506); Retinal degeneration (HP:0000506) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal outer nuclear layer of the retina (HP:0012009); Retinal degeneration (HP:0000506) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal outer nuclear layer of the retina (HP:0012009). Mutations in CLRN1 disrupt the endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein degradation (ERAD) pathway, leading to the accumulation of misfolded proteins and cellular stress within photoreceptor cells. This ultimately results in retinal degeneration, manifesting as abnormal outer nuclear layers in both Bardet-Biedl syndrome and retinitis pigmentosa 61.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in CLRN1 associated with a loss-of-function mechanism in both diseases would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if mutations in CLRN1 were found to be associated with a gain-of-function mechanism in one disease, or if distinct genes were identified as the primary cause of either disease with no overlap in functional consequence, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a significantly higher frequency of loss-of-function variants in CLRN1 in patients with these diseases compared to the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of CLRN1 dysfunction in ERAD provides a common therapeutic target for both Bardet-Biedl syndrome and retinitis pigmentosa 61, potentially leading to treatments that mitigate photoreceptor degeneration.
